{"user":"I’m planning a weekend trip to Lisbon for two people in late September. Can you suggest a 3-day itinerary with neighborhoods to stay in, and include a short list of “must-see” spots plus one nice dinner reservation idea for each night?","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a complete 3-day Lisbon plan for two people in late September, including where to stay, must-sees, and dinner ideas each night. I’ll also coordinate the routing so you’re not zig-zagging across town each day.

Where to stay (neighborhoods)
- Baixa / Chiado: most convenient for first-timers; walkable to major sights; easy transit.
- Alfama: atmospheric and scenic (more hills/steps); great for an “old Lisbon” feel.
- Príncipe Real / Avenida da Liberdade: stylish, calmer evenings, good restaurants and parks.
- Cais do Sodré (choose streets away from nightlife): good access to waterfront and transit.

Must-see shortlist
- Belém Tower (Torre de Belém)
- Jerónimos Monastery (Mosteiro dos Jerónimos)
- Alfama viewpoints (Miradouros) such as Portas do Sol / Santa Luzia
- São Jorge Castle
- Tram 28 ride (even if partial)
- LX Factory (daytime wandering)
- Time Out Market (quick, varied food options)

Day 1 — Historic core + viewpoints (easy pace)
- Morning: Start in Baixa/Chiado; wander up toward Rossio.
- Late morning: Alfama stroll + Igreja de Santo António.
- Lunch: choose a small taverna in Alfama or Mouraria.
- Afternoon: Miradouro stops (Portas do Sol → Santa Luzia) and then São Jorge Castle.
- Evening dinner idea (reservation): a fado-focused dinner show in Alfama/nearby—look for a place that has dinner + a set time (I can help narrow options based on your vibe).

Day 2 — Belém + riverside + LX Factory
- Morning: Belém Tower + riverside promenade.
- Late morning: Jerónimos Monastery.
- Lunch: try a classic custard pastry experience around Belém and a simple nearby lunch.
- Afternoon: walk into the cultural hub around MAAT / gardens area, then head to LX Factory for shops and a casual drink.
- Evening dinner idea (reservation): a modern Portuguese spot in the Alcântara/Belém-to-city axis, or a well-reviewed seafood dinner near the river.

Day 3 — Modern Lisbon + a scenic day finale
- Morning: Tram 28 (or a partial route) + Estrela/Basilica area if you want something calmer than the densest tourist blocks.
- Lunch: Time Out Market (good for sampling and minimal planning).
- Afternoon: Príncipe Real gardens (or nearby viewpoints) and stroll Avenida da Liberdade.
- Evening dinner idea (reservation): a Portuguese restaurant in Chiado/Bairro Alto with seasonal tasting options.

To make this truly plug-and-play, tell me two things and I’ll tighten the itinerary with exact walk order and “best time to go” notes:
1) Where will you start from (airport/hotel area) and what time do you arrive/depart?
2) Do you prefer fado/dining shows, or would you rather keep evenings purely restaurant-focused?","minus_response":"Sure—here’s a simple 3-day Lisbon itinerary with a few key sights and one dinner idea each night.

Where to stay (pick one)
- Baixa/Chiado (most convenient)
- Alfama (prettiest/most scenic, more hills)
- Príncipe Real (nice and a bit calmer)

Must-sees
Belém Tower, Jerónimos Monastery, Alfama viewpoints, São Jorge Castle, Tram 28.

Day 1
- Alfama + viewpoints (Portas do Sol / Santa Luzia)
- São Jorge Castle
- Dinner: a fado dinner spot in/near Alfama.

Day 2
- Belém Tower + Jerónimos Monastery
- LX Factory (walk around)
- Dinner: seafood or modern Portuguese near the river (reservations recommended).

Day 3
- Tram 28 (partial is fine)
- Time Out Market for lunch
- Príncipe Real stroll
- Dinner: a strong Portuguese restaurant in Chiado/Bairro Alto.

If you want, give me your arrival/departure times and whether you want fado or not, and you can fill in the exact restaurant names yourself for the reservation slots."}
